maker.featuresTitle: A sprite sheet generator built around your frame sequence

features.title: GIF to sprite sheet, with complete frames
features.text: A GIF can store only the pixels that change between frames. The GIF to sprite sheet workflow reconstructs the full image for each moment, including transparent areas and frame disposal. Original frame timing stays available for animation preview and JSON export; you can override it with a consistent FPS when needed.

features.title: Combine images without stretching them
features.text: When you combine images into a sprite sheet, the largest source width and height define the grid cell. Smaller images keep their original dimensions. Bottom-center alignment helps characters share a ground line, while center and top-left alignment suit effects or interface assets. Transparent source margins stay intact unless you turn on Crop transparent edges.

features.title: Preview the animation before exporting
features.text: Switch between the full sheet and sprite sheet animation preview to inspect both layout and motion. Pause on a frame, step forward or backward, and compare timing. Pixelated display keeps small sprites crisp; preview zoom changes what you see, not the resolution of the exported PNG.

If a character still appears to jump vertically, inspect the transparent margins in the source frames; alignment cannot infer the location of the feet.

useCases.text: Use horizontal strips for small effects, or a compact grid for icons and animation frames. GIF input is useful when the animation already exists as one file. This sprite sheet creator packages existing artwork; it does not invent in-between frames or turn a still image into a new animated character.

maker.guideTitle: Sprite sheet settings and export details

guide.title: Columns, margins, and frame spacing
guide.text: Columns control how many cells appear across a grid. Outer margin adds empty space around the sheet, while frame gap separates neighboring cells. These are different settings: importing the wrong gap into an engine can make the next sprite bleed into a frame. The displayed output dimensions update as you adjust the layout.

guide.title: Transparent PNG and JSON coordinates
guide.text: The default export background is transparent; a selected solid color is baked into the PNG. JSON uses a TexturePacker-style hash with unique filenames, source dimensions, frame rectangles, and duration. You can also export JSON Array, CSS, XML, or an animated GIF in the same ZIP. PNG grid slicing and JSON atlas import are different workflows; see the engine notes in the export panel.

Each source image or output sheet is limited to 8192 pixels per edge and 16 million pixels. Reduce dimensions or split a long animation if a limit is reached. Refreshing the page clears the workspace.

features.text: The sprite sheet cutter supports two ways to describe a regular grid. features.text: A single sheet may contain several actions and unused cells. guide.title: Offsets and gaps solve different problems
guide.text: An offset moves the first cutting cell away from the left or top image edge. A gap skips pixels between cells. Right and bottom margins can exclude an outer border, including margins passed from Maker. If every cut drifts farther from the artwork across a row, check the horizontal gap rather than shifting the entire grid.

guide.title: Understand unused edges and invalid grids
guide.text: Cells use whole pixels. When an image does not divide evenly, the tool reports unused pixels at the right and bottom instead of stretching the frames or silently treating a partial cell as complete. A grid that cannot fit a full frame blocks export. Recheck the dimensions against your source before accepting the preview.

faq.text: No. The current pipeline includes background removal and normalization into square cells. Preview the result before using it in your game, especially for translucent effects, thin objects, or clips with several overlapping subjects.

faq.title: Can I download individual PNG frames?
faq.text: Yes. Select cells in the result workspace and download one PNG or a ZIP. You can also download the complete sprite sheet. Check frame selection before exporting so unused transparent grid cells are not treated as part of the action.

faq.title: What does animation FPS change?
faq.text: It supplies the initial result playback speed and is passed to the processor, which derives a bounded candidate sampling rate from it. The preview FPS can subsequently be adjusted locally. Submitting new extraction settings is a separate explicit action.

background.title: Free Transparent Background Maker
background.intro: Use this transparent background maker to cut game characters, props, and item artwork out of their backgrounds. Process up to 20 images locally, compare before and after, and download transparent PNGs. Your images never leave your device; only the model needs an initial download.
background.stepsTitle: How to use transparent background maker

steps.title: Choose one image or a small batch
steps.text: Add PNG, JPEG, or static WebP files to the transparent background maker. Each image can be up to 10 MiB, with a maximum of 20 images in the workspace. Start with a clear subject and enough contrast around its edges. No account or project is required.

steps.title: Download the model once, then process
steps.text: On first use, the transparent background maker downloads the IS-Net model and displays real download progress. Inference then runs in a browser worker, one image at a time. Cached weights can be reused on later visits and by the GIF tool; your artwork is not part of that cache.

steps.title: Compare and save the useful results
steps.text: Select a result and drag the before-and-after divider to inspect the silhouette. The transparent background maker provides individual PNG downloads and a ZIP of completed files. A failed image can be retried separately without repeating successful work. Download everything you need before closing the tab.

features.title: Local inference for unreleased game artwork
features.text: This transparent background maker keeps source images and output pixels inside your browser. No image-upload request is needed for segmentation. Model and runtime files are downloaded from our storage, so first use needs an internet connection; local processing does not mean that all page resources are available offline.

features.title: Batch cleanup without losing individual control
features.text: The transparent background maker processes up to 20 files sequentially to limit memory pressure. Each item shows its own state and can be inspected after completion. Download one finished prop while other files continue, or collect the successful PNGs in a ZIP when the batch is ready.

features.title: Before-and-after checks at original dimensions
features.text: The transparent background maker restores the predicted mask to the source dimensions and retains existing alpha transparency. Compare the original against a checkerboard result to find missing outlines, holes, or unwanted shadows. Automatic segmentation is a starting point; very fine details may still require an image editor.

useCases.title: Prepare character portraits and inventory items
useCases.text: Use a transparent background maker for your own character portraits, potion bottles, weapons, and collectible artwork. Transparent PNGs can sit over different interface panels without a rectangular backdrop. Inspect narrow handles, antennae, and small decorative elements before adding the asset to a production inventory.

useCases.title: Clean sprites and pixel-art studies
useCases.text: Try the tool as a sprite background remover or pixel art background remover when the foreground is clearly separated. A sprite sheet background remover must distinguish every desired object from the backdrop, so crowded sheets can be harder than individual sprites. Check outlines at normal game scale as well as enlarged.

guide.title: Supported images and output format
guide.text: The transparent background maker accepts PNG, JPEG, and static WebP. The output is a PNG at the original image dimensions, even for a JPEG input. Animated WebP and GIF are not batch still-image formats here; use GIF Background Remover when each animation frame needs its own mask.

guide.title: Transparent pixels are not a background color
guide.text: A transparent PNG contains an alpha channel. The checkerboard is only a preview and is not baked into your download. When checking a pixel art transparent background, view it against both light and dark surfaces so leftover edge colors are easier to notice.

guide.title: First download and browser cache
guide.text: The IS-Net model is about 170.4 MiB. Progress shows transferred bytes, followed by a separate initialization stage. If browser storage is unavailable or cleared, another visit may need another download. The transparent background maker does not save your source images or processing session across refreshes.

guide.title: Memory and difficult edges
guide.text: A file-size limit is not a promise that every device can process every image. Large decoded images and model initialization both use memory. Use smaller images if necessary. Smoke, glass, disconnected effects, and subjects blending into the background are harder cases; compare results before replacing your originals.

background.faqText: Answers to check before processing and downloading your assets.

faq.title: Is this transparent background maker free?
faq.text: Yes. You can remove backgrounds, compare results, and download PNGs or a ZIP without signing in or spending credits. The separate AI generation workspace is optional and is not needed to use this tool.

faq.title: Are my images uploaded to your server?
faq.text: No. The browser downloads model resources and runs image segmentation locally. Source images and processed PNGs stay on your device. The separate video conversion tool uses uploads and server processing, so its privacy behavior is different.

faq.title: Can I process 20 images together?
faq.text: Yes, with a maximum of 10 MiB per image. They are processed sequentially, with a status for each file. Successful images remain downloadable if another image fails; retry the failed item instead of starting the entire batch again.

faq.title: Will pixel-art edges remain perfectly crisp?
faq.text: The model predicts a foreground mask and can soften or remove small details. Check the result at your game’s actual display size. This tool does not guarantee pixel-perfect segmentation or replace manual cleanup of individual pixels.

faq.title: Can I download a JPG with transparency?
faq.text: JPEG does not support an alpha channel. Download the PNG result to preserve the transparent background. Keep the original if you plan to compare the mask or retry with a different source crop later.

gifBackground.title: Free GIF Background Remover
gifBackground.intro: Use a GIF background remover that processes every frame in your browser. Compare the original motion with the cutout, then download a transparent GIF, sprite sheet, or PNG sequence. Your animation is never uploaded; the shared IS-Net model runs locally on your device.
gifBackground.stepsTitle: How to use gif background remover

steps.title: Open a short game animation
steps.text: Choose one GIF up to 10 MiB in the GIF background remover. The decoder first rebuilds complete frames, including partial updates and disposal rules. A maximum of 256 frames and 32 million decoded pixels keeps the workload bounded. Short character loops are a practical starting point.

steps.title: Prepare the model and remove each background
steps.text: The GIF background remover downloads IS-Net on first use and shows the transferred bytes. After initialization, it processes frames sequentially while preserving their original dimensions and timing. A cached model can be shared with Transparent Background Maker, but your animation itself is not saved in that cache.

steps.title: Compare motion and choose an export
steps.text: Play the synchronized before-and-after preview, or pause on a difficult frame. Once every frame succeeds, the GIF background remover can export a transparent GIF, PNG sprite sheet, or ZIP of PNG frames. Retry a failed frame without silently omitting it from the final animation.

features.title: Private processing for animated game assets
features.text: This GIF background remover runs image segmentation in a browser worker. It downloads the model and runtime resources but does not send your GIF or frame pixels to an image API. Keep the tab open during processing, especially on devices where initializing the model takes longer.

features.title: One canvas size across the whole action
features.text: The GIF background remover preserves the source canvas instead of independently cropping every silhouette. Stable dimensions help avoid artificial jumps when a sword swings outward or a character leans. Original GIF frame delays stay attached to the sequence; background removal does not invent new transition frames.

features.title: Synchronized before and after
features.text: Use the GIF background remover comparison to inspect the same moment in both versions. Pause, step through the timeline, and drag the divider across the character. Look for disappearing effects and changing outlines: an image model evaluates frames individually, so temporal consistency is not guaranteed.

useCases.title: Character loops for prototypes
useCases.text: Use a GIF background remover on your own idle, walk, or attack animations before placing them over a new game scene. Transparent frames are useful for prototype motion tests and animation editors. Check feet, weapons, and accessories throughout the entire action rather than judging only the first frame.

useCases.title: Effects, animated items, and UI previews
useCases.text: Try the tool on an isolated animated object, collectible, or effect preview. Clearly separated foregrounds are easier than smoke or glowing particles blended into a scene. The PNG sequence is useful when you want to retouch individual masks before packing the final game asset.

guide.title: GIF transparency versus PNG alpha
guide.text: A GIF background remover can export a transparent GIF, but GIF supports a single transparent palette entry rather than smooth alpha levels. Soft edges may become harder after encoding. Choose a PNG sprite sheet or PNG frames when your game needs partially transparent pixels and more faithful edge blending.

guide.title: Frame timing and sheet layout
guide.text: Transparent GIF export keeps the recovered per-frame delays, within GIF timing precision. The sheet uses a regular grid, while the ZIP contains ordered PNG frames. A PNG alone does not store playback timing. Use GIF to Sprite Sheet if you need additional layout controls and metadata exports.

guide.title: Download, initialization, and cancellation
guide.text: The shared model is about 170.4 MiB. The GIF background remover shows download progress separately from model initialization and frame processing. Cancel stops the active browser worker. Completed results remain in the current session, so you can retry the remaining work without accepting an incomplete animation.

guide.title: Limits and visual cleanup
guide.text: Compressed GIF size does not describe decoded memory use. Large dimensions or many frames can exceed the pixel budget even below 10 MiB. Shorten or resize the animation when necessary. Automatic masks can flicker between frames; inspect outlines and translucent effects before replacing the source artwork.

gifBackground.faqText: Answers to check before processing and downloading your assets.

faq.title: Is this GIF background remover free without an account?
faq.text: Yes. Local background removal, comparison, and all three export formats are free. There is no project requirement or generation-credit charge. The first model download needs a connection, and processing speed depends on your device.

faq.title: Does my GIF leave the browser?
faq.text: No. The tool downloads its model resources and processes the decoded animation locally. Your source GIF and transparent frames are not uploaded. Do not confuse this with the video converter, which explicitly uses server processing.

faq.title: Can I export a sprite sheet instead of a GIF?
faq.text: Yes. Download a transparent PNG sheet or a ZIP of ordered PNG frames after all frames finish. These formats preserve full alpha transparency and avoid GIF palette limitations. The original frame dimensions remain consistent throughout the sequence.

faq.title: Why does a glow look different in the GIF download?
faq.text: GIF cannot represent smooth partial transparency, and its palette is limited. A soft glow may have a harder boundary after encoding. Compare the PNG output as well; even there, model segmentation may need manual correction around translucent effects.

faq.title: What happens if one frame fails?
faq.text: The failed frame is marked and can be retried. Full animation exports stay disabled until every frame has a result, so an error cannot quietly remove a pose from your animation. Successful frames remain available in the current tab.
